title: Let my people go (Exodus 5)
hook: the first demand, and Pharaoh makes the bricks harder to make

segments.voice: Yesterday, ehyeh: I will be with you, God's answer to a man slow of speech. Your line was slow of speech, still sent. This week ran from two brave midwives to a basket, a prince who saw, a bush, a name, and a reluctant prophet. Today he finally walks into the palace.

You know these four words even if you've never opened the book of Exodus. Enslaved people in America sang them in the fields: go down, Moses, tell old Pharaoh, let my people go. People marching for freedom have painted them on signs. But the first time they were said, in the Torah, two brothers carried them into a throne room: Moses and Aaron, standing before the king of Egypt. Aaron speaking, Moses beside him.
screen: `GO DOWN, MOSES.` → `TWO BROTHERS IN A THRONE ROOM.` → `THE FIRST TIME IT'S SAID.`

segments.voice: They say: thus says the LORD, the God of Israel, "Let My people go, that they may hold a feast unto Me in the wilderness." Pharaoh answers with a sneer: "Who is the LORD, that I should hearken unto His voice?" I don't know him, and I won't let Israel go. Then he does what every tyrant knows how to do. That same day, he gives the taskmasters a new order: stop giving the people straw to make bricks. Let them gather it themselves, and keep the number of bricks the same. They're lazy, he says; that's why they're crying, let us go. Make the work heavier, so they won't listen to lies. The people scatter all over Egypt looking for stubble. They can't keep up. The Israelite foremen are beaten. And who do they blame? Not Pharaoh. Moses and Aaron. You've made us stink in Pharaoh's eyes, they say; you've put a sword in their hand to kill us. Moses turns to God, and he doesn't hold back. Why have you done evil to this people? Why did you ever send me? Since I came, it's only gotten worse. The first try failed. The people turned on their leader, and the leader turned to God with a complaint. And God doesn't scold him. God says: now you'll see what I'll do to Pharaoh. The next chapter says the people couldn't even listen, because of their crushed spirit and hard labor. The Hebrew is kotzer ruach, shortness of breath. That's what it feels like when it gets harder first.
screen: `LET MY PEOPLE GO.` · `WHO IS THE LORD?` · `NO STRAW, SAME BRICKS.` · `WHY DID YOU EVER SEND ME?` · then, large: `IT GETS HARDER FIRST.`

segments.voice: Think of something you tried recently that didn't work, or made things worse: a hard conversation, a new habit, a plan that fell apart. Let the voice that says why did I even start have its say, the way Moses did. Then picture what a second try might look like; you don't have to do it today.
Kotzer ruach, shortness of breath, the Hebrew the Torah uses for the people who couldn't even listen, crushed by labor after the first demand made things harder.
Your line: it gets harder first. Even Moses asked why he'd been sent. Tomorrow, the plagues.

howItsDone: At the Passover seder Jews retell the slavery in Egypt as their own story, and the words let my people go have been taken up by many freedom movements, including the African American spiritual Go Down, Moses.
